result.summary: Introduces a minimal `linux-base-gcc` toolchain variant in Guix for non-GUI static Linux builds, disabling unused `libstdc++` features (`--disable-wchar_t`, `--enable-clocale=generic`, and `--with-libstdcxx-zoneinfo=no`). It also disables the experimental `libstdc++fs` library across Linux GCC builds and adds a patch in `depends` so Boost Test compiles without `std::wcrtomb`.
result.problem: Guix non-GUI Linux release binaries link unused `libstdc++` components such as wide-character handling, timezone info, and the experimental filesystem TS library, unnecessarily inflating binary sizes.
evidence: Author measurements demonstrate ~0.48 MB size reductions across non-GUI binaries (bitcoind drops from 17.75 MB to 17.27 MB, bitcoin-cli from 8.20 MB to 7.72 MB).
result.changed_since_previous: Dropped commits associated with PR #36531 (including changes to Guix module loading via `--load-path`), removing the dependency on that PR.
result.card: Introduces a minimal linux-base-gcc toolchain variant for non-GUI Linux static Guix builds, disabling unused libstdc++ features including wide-character support, zoneinfo, and the filesystem TS library. It also patches Boost Test in depends to invoke wcrtomb without std namespace qualification to maintain compatibility without wchar_t support. This reduces release binary sizes for tools like bitcoind and bitcoin-cli by roughly 0.5 MB.

risk.why: Altering GCC libstdc++ compilation flags affects release binaries and could cause runtime breakages if non-GUI code relies on disabled standard library features.
